questions.stem_latex:
Consider the curve $y=ax^2+bx+c$, where $a\ne 0$.

At a particular point, the tangent and normal to the curve are given by

$t(x)=5(x+1)$ and $n(x)=-\dfrac{x}{5}-\dfrac{1}{5}$ respectively.

The curve has a maximum turning point at $x=\dfrac{1}{4}$

parts.label: a
parts.latex: Show that the point of intersection of the tangent and the normal is $(-1,0)$

parts.label: b
parts.latex: Find the values of $a$, $b$ and $c$.

solutions.latex:
Replacing $x$ by $\dfrac{x}{2}$ stretches the graph horizontally by a factor of 2.

Subtracting 9 from the function moves the graph down 9 units.

Answer: (A)

The graph passes through $(0,0)$, has vertical asymptotes $x=\pm 2$ and horizontal asymptote $y=1$.

$y=\dfrac{x^2}{x^2-4}$: zero at $x=0$, undefined at $x=\pm2$, and $y\to 1$ as $x\to\pm\infty$. (D) tends to $-1$; (A) tends to $0$; (C) is undefined at $x=0$.

Answer: (B)
$$\begin{aligned} y'&=e^x(\sec^2 x)+\tan x\times e^x\\ &=e^x(\sec^2 x+\tan x)\end{aligned}$$

$$\cos 2x=\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}$$

$-\pi\le x\le\pi$, so $-2\pi\le 2x\le 2\pi$

related acute angle $=\dfrac{\pi}{6}$ (cosine positive in quadrants 1 and 4)

\exfigure{644_q9_s1}

$$2x=\frac{\pi}{6},\ 2\pi-\frac{\pi}{6},\ -\frac{\pi}{6},\ -\left(2\pi-\frac{\pi}{6}\right)$$

$$2x=\frac{\pi}{6},\ \frac{11\pi}{6},\ -\frac{\pi}{6},\ -\frac{11\pi}{6}$$

$$x=\frac{\pi}{12},\ \frac{11\pi}{12},\ -\frac{\pi}{12},\ -\frac{11\pi}{12}$$

solutions.latex:
$$y=\frac{1+\sin x}{\cos x}$$

$$\begin{aligned} y'&=\frac{\cos x(\cos x)-(-\sin x)(1+\sin x)}{\cos^2 x}\\ &=\frac{\cos^2 x+\sin x+\sin^2 x}{\cos^2 x}\\ &=\frac{1+\sin x}{\cos^2 x}\end{aligned}$$

$$\sec x+\tan x=\frac{1}{\cos x}+\frac{\sin x}{\cos x}=\frac{1+\sin x}{\cos x}$$

$$f(x)=\frac{1+\sin x}{\cos x},\quad f'(x)=\frac{1+\sin x}{\cos^2 x}\ \text{(from part a)}$$

$$\begin{aligned}\frac{d}{dx}\ln(\sec x+\tan x)&=\frac{d}{dx}\ln\left(\frac{1+\sin x}{\cos x}\right)\\ &=\frac{1+\sin x}{\cos^2 x}\times\frac{\cos x}{1+\sin x}\\ &=\frac{1}{\cos x}=\sec x\end{aligned}$$

Hence proved.

solutions.latex:
$$V=s\left(100s-s^2\left(\frac{\pi+4}{4}\right)\right)$$

$$V=100s^2-s^3\left(\frac{\pi+4}{4}\right)$$

$$\frac{dV}{ds}=200s-3s^2\left(\frac{\pi+4}{4}\right)$$

Sub $\dfrac{dV}{ds}=0$:

$$200s-3s^2\left(\frac{\pi+4}{4}\right)=0$$

$$s\left(200-3s\left(\frac{\pi+4}{4}\right)\right)=0$$

$s=0$, $\quad 200=3s\left(\dfrac{\pi+4}{4}\right)$

$$s=\frac{200\times4}{3(\pi+4)}\approx 37.34$$

$$\frac{d^2V}{ds^2}=200-6s\left(\frac{\pi+4}{4}\right)$$

$\dfrac{d^2V}{ds^2}(37.34)\approx-200<0$, concave down, maximum turning point

$\therefore s=37.34$ will give maximum volume.
solutions.marks_breakdown: 1: correct volume expression; 1: calculated the value of s; 1: showed that the value of s will give the maximum volume

solutions.latex:
Equate $t(x)$ and $n(x)$:

$$5(x+1)=-\frac{x}{5}-\frac{1}{5}$$

$$5(5x+5)=-x-1$$

$$25x+25=-x-1$$

$$25x+x=-1-25$$

$$26x=-26,\quad x=-1$$

$t(-1)=5(-1+1)=0$

$\therefore$ the point of intersection of the tangent and the normal is $(-1,0)$.

$$y=ax^2+bx+c,\quad y'=2ax+b$$

Gradient of tangent and the curve is same at $(-1,0)$:

$$2a(-1)+b=5$$

$$-2a+b=5\quad (1)$$

Max TP at $x=\dfrac{1}{4}$, $\therefore y'\left(\dfrac{1}{4}\right)=0$

$$2a\left(\frac{1}{4}\right)+b=0$$

$$\frac{a}{2}+b=0\quad (2)$$

Subtract (1) from (2):

$$\frac{a}{2}+2a=-5,\quad \frac{5a}{2}=-5,\quad a=-\frac{5\times2}{5}=-2$$

$$\frac{a}{2}+b=0,\quad b=-\frac{a}{2}=1$$

For $c$, sub any point, $a$ and $b$ in the general equation $y=ax^2+bx+c$; sub $(-1,0)$:

$$0=-2(-1)^2+1(-1)+c$$

$$c-1-2=0,\quad c=3$$

$\therefore a=-2,\ b=1,\ c=3$
solutions.marks_breakdown: 1: using the gradient of tangent; 1: using the gradient at the TP; 1: substituting the POI in the quadratic equation (fourth mark not itemised in source)
